text: March, nineteen eighty-nine. Mark Kilroy, a twenty-one-year-old pre-med student from the University of Texas, crossed into Mah-tah-mor-ohs for spring break with his friends.
text0: March 1989. Mark Kilroy, a twenty-one-year-old pre-med student from the University of Texas, crossed into Matamoros for spring break with his friends.

text: Fifteen thousand spring breakers crowded the streets that night. Around two in the morning, outside a bar, Mark vanished.
His friends searched until dawn. His parents printed twenty thousand flyers, offered a fifteen-thousand-dollar reward, and took the case to national television. For weeks, nothing.
Then, on April first, a drug trafficker named Seh-rah-feen Er-nahn-dez drove straight through a police checkpoint. According to later accounts, he believed rituals had made him invisible.
text0: Then, on April 1st, a drug trafficker named Serafín Hernández drove straight through a police checkpoint. According to later accounts, he believed rituals had made him invisible.

text: Federal police followed him to a ranch outside the city: Rancho Santa Elena. Inside, they found ritual objects and traces of drugs.
Days later, they arrested Serafín, his uncle Eh-lee-oh, and three others. Serafín confessed: people had been killed at the ranch, on the orders of a man they called El Pah-dree-no.
text0: Days later, they arrested Serafín, his uncle Elio, and three others. Serafín confessed: people had been killed at the ranch, on the orders of a man they called El Padrino.

text: Police dug up a ritual cauldron… and fifteen bodies, most of them rival traffickers. One of them was Mark Kilroy.
El Pah-dree-no was Adolfo de Heh-soos Kon-stahn-zo, born in Miami in nineteen sixty-two. His mother practiced Pah-lo Mah-yom-beh, and he grew up steeped in ritual.
text0: El Padrino was Adolfo de Jesús Constanzo, born in Miami in 1962. His mother practiced Palo Mayombe, and he grew up steeped in ritual.

text: In Mexico City, he read tarot cards for wealthy clients, among them drug dealers and, reportedly, corrupt police.

Then he made a deal with a trafficking family: a share of their profits, in exchange for his protection. He promised his followers that human sacrifice would protect them from bullets and from the police.
His second-in-command was Sara Al-dreh-teh, a top student from just across the border. Followers called her, La Mah-dree-nah.
text0: His second-in-command was Sara Aldrete, a top student from just across the border. Followers called her La Madrina.

text: Weeks later, police cornered Kon-stahn-zo in Mexico City. On May sixth, nineteen eighty-nine, he ordered one of his own followers to shoot him.
text0: Weeks later, police cornered Constanzo in Mexico City. On May 6th, 1989, he ordered one of his own followers to shoot him.

text: Al-dreh-teh was arrested at the scene. In nineteen ninety-four, she was sentenced to more than sixty years in prison. She still insists she is innocent.
text0: Aldrete was arrested at the scene. In 1994, she was sentenced to more than sixty years in prison. She still insists she is innocent.

text: Mark's parents started a foundation in his name, teaching young people about the dangers of drugs.
No trial for El Pah-dree-no. No answers. The cult that thought it was invisible was exposed by the one family that wouldn't stop looking. This is Plot Twist, with A. and R.
